description: Ten polyphonic sample and hold rows, normalled so that consecutive rows work together as an analogue shift register

params.text: Sets oversampling to off, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x or 32x, cutting aliasing when the sample and hold is triggered at audio rates
Sets the range of the internal random generator: 0-1V, 0-5V, 0-10V, or the bipolar 1V, 5V and 10V pairs
Triggers a sample on the first row
Resets every polyphonic channel of all ten HOLD outputs to 0V

inputs.text: A rise above 2V samples the first row's DATA voltage, and the trigger counts as low again below 0.1V
A rise above 2V samples that row's DATA voltage, and the trigger counts as low again below 0.1V; unpatched it takes the TRIG input of the row above
The voltage the first row samples; unpatched it is normalled to a fresh random value
The voltage that row samples; with the row's TRIG patched it is normalled to a fresh random value, and with TRIG unpatched to the HOLD output of the row above

outputs.text: Carries the last value that row sampled, held until its next trigger

notes: patching a lower row rather than the top one leaves the rows above it idle, which costs far less CPU while oversampling is on
menu: Save held values — on by default, storing the held values with the patch and restoring them on load; switch it off and the rows come back empty
Oversample filter quality — 10th order by default, with 8th order and a cheaper 6th order; 10th and 8th cut at 80% of Nyquist and 6th at 50%
